Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old woman with 3-week history of left-sided hearing loss and facial numbness, possibly Bell’s palsy; urgent in-person assessment and neurological examination advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Problems with hearing and numbness of the face.
- Symptom details:
  - Onset: Approximately 3 weeks ago.
  - Nature: Left-sided hearing loss, numbness around the left ear and jawline; ongoing and persistent at time of consult.
  - Associated symptoms: Occasional ringing (tinnitus) in left ear, sometimes associated with dizziness. No ear discharge, ear pain, fever, or itchiness. No weakness or numbness elsewhere in the body. No difficulty swallowing or speaking. No visual disturbances.
  - Aggravating/relieving factors: Not mentioned.
  - Impact: Symptoms impacting ability to train and work as a jockey.
- Systems review: No additional neurologic, cardiovascular, or respiratory symptoms reported. Negative review for fever, weakness elsewhere, swallowing, and speech difficulties.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps; uses nasal spray as needed (name not recalled).
- Occasional use of Rennies (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Prior history of labyrinthitis (“ages ago,” no ongoing issues).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- Medications:
  - Nasal spray for polyps (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Rennies (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Latex.

Social History:
- Occupation: Jockey (horse riding); work performance impacted by symptoms.
- Living situation: Lives with partner (initially said lives alone, then corrected to living with partner; conflict noted).
- No pets.
- Smoking, alcohol, or substance use: Not mentioned.

Family History:
- Brother with neurofibromatosis.
- No other relevant family illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (video consultation).

Investigations:
- None performed during consult; no results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss and facial numbness, possible Bell’s palsy.
  - Plan: Urgent same-day in-person clinic visit for physical and neurological examination to confirm diagnosis. Ear examination recommended.
- General plan items:
  - Reassured patient that life-threatening conditions are unlikely, but further clinical assessment needed for definitive reassurance.
  - Patient to call support team to arrange face-to-face appointment in Central London today.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements for a consult:
  - Full medication reconciliation (names/doses/frequency/indications for all medicines).
  - Smoking, alcohol, and other substance use history.
  - Full review of systems.
  - Recent vitals and physical examination findings.
  - More detail regarding nasal spray.
  - Surgical history not provided.
●	Conflicts in transcript:
  - Living situation: Initially states lives alone, then says lives with partner. (Conflict noted.)
●	Transcript quality:
  - Clear and complete for primary complaint and associated history. Minor conversational repetition and small gaps; overall good quality.
